_comment: pay_per_container_nm: a ship is paid capacity x leg distance (nm) x this rate when it finishes unloading; tuned so a Scooter 10 earns about $2,000 per minute of sailing. fuel_price: dollars per fuel unit, the same at every port (fuel is about 40% of a leg's pay). Breakdowns: every breakdown_interval_s seconds there's a breakdown_chance that one random ship at sea (not a recovery boat) loses breakdown_hit of its maintenance (0.5 = 50 points). initial_view_width_deg: how many degrees of longitude the map shows across when it opens, centered on the home port.
_xp_comment: XP: every delivery (when unloading finishes) gives the company and the ship capacity x leg distance (nm) x xp_per_container_nm. Company levels run 1 to max_company_level. Level L costs (company_level_minutes[0] + company_level_minutes[1] x (L - 1)) minutes of the XP a full fleet at that level would earn at sea (at_sea_share of the time): the best unlocked cargo models, max_owned of each, filling fleet_slots. So each level takes about as long no matter how big the fleet has become, and level 100 takes about 40 hours. fleet_slots: [company level, cargo ship slots] benchmarks; recovery boats don't use slots. Ships level 0 to ship_max_level, one skill point per level; see ship_models.json xp_first_level and ship_level_growth. skills: the bonus per skill level (speed: top speed +2%; durability: wear and breakdown chance -5%; efficiency: fuel burn -3%), up to skill_max_level each.
